jungian_shadow.name: Jungian Shadow
jungian_shadow.description: The shadow contains traits, impulses, and feelings the ego has rejected as incompatible with its self-image. What we cannot accept in ourselves we project onto others — seeing in them what we refuse to see in ourselves. The shadow is not inherently negative; it holds both destructive patterns and unlived potential.
jungian_shadow.protocol_note: Shadow work involves owning the projected quality — not as a flaw to fix, but as a disowned part to integrate.

attachment_anxious.name: Anxious Attachment
attachment_anxious.description: Anxious attachment develops when caregiving was inconsistent — sometimes available, sometimes not. The person learns that connection is possible but unreliable, producing hypervigilance to relational signals, fear of abandonment, and a tendency to amplify bids for connection. Underneath is a core belief: 'I am not enough to be chosen consistently.'
attachment_anxious.protocol_note: The activation pattern is threat-detection in neutral relational events. The intervention point is before the bid for reassurance, not after rejection.

attachment_avoidant.name: Avoidant Attachment
attachment_avoidant.description: Avoidant attachment develops when emotional needs were consistently unmet or dismissed. The person learns that relying on others is unsafe and builds a self-sufficient identity as protection. Intimacy is approached with ambivalence — desired but threatening. The core belief: 'I am safer alone.'
attachment_avoidant.protocol_note: The pattern activates at the moment of potential vulnerability — before asking for help, before disclosing difficulty. That is the intervention point.

fawn_response.name: Fawn Response
fawn_response.description: The fawn response is a survival strategy in which the person appeases, agrees, and accommodates to avoid conflict or threat. It is a nervous system response, not a personality trait — the body learned that compliance reduces danger. Over time it becomes automatic, operating even in low-stakes situations where no real threat exists.
fawn_response.protocol_note: The fawn response bypasses conscious choice — it fires before the person decides to agree. Detection must happen in the body, before the words come out.

inner_critic.name: Inner Critic
inner_critic.description: The inner critic is a protective part that attacks the self before the outside world can. Its logic: if I find my flaws first, I control the exposure. The criticism feels like truth but is actually a preemptive defence. The critic's harshness is proportional to the wound it is trying to protect.
inner_critic.protocol_note: The critic speaks in absolutes — always, never, everyone can see. These linguistic markers are the detection trigger. The intervention is not to silence the critic but to ask what it is protecting.

cognitive_distortion_catastrophising.name: Catastrophising
cognitive_distortion_catastrophising.description: Catastrophising is the pattern of assuming the worst possible outcome when faced with uncertainty. It functions as a control strategy — if I imagine the worst, I will not be caught off guard. The payoff is a sense of preparation; the cost is chronic anxiety and avoidance of situations where failure is possible.
cognitive_distortion_catastrophising.protocol_note: The intervention is not positive thinking but probability testing — what is the realistic likelihood of this outcome, and what would actually happen if it occurred?

core_belief_unworthiness.name: Core Belief — Unworthiness
core_belief_unworthiness.description: A core belief of unworthiness operates as a lens through which all experience is interpreted. Successes are dismissed as luck or deception; failures confirm the belief. The person structures their behaviour to avoid situations that might expose the unworthiness — which also prevents the disconfirming experiences that would challenge it.
core_belief_unworthiness.protocol_note: The belief is maintained by selective attention — noticing confirming evidence, dismissing disconfirming evidence. The protocol must target the dismissal mechanism, not the belief directly.

identity_foreclosure.name: Identity Foreclosure
identity_foreclosure.description: Identity foreclosure occurs when a person adopts a fixed identity without exploration — often to meet external expectations or to resolve anxiety quickly. The foreclosed identity feels certain but brittle; it cannot accommodate new information about the self. 'I'm just not someone who...' is its linguistic signature.
identity_foreclosure.protocol_note: The foreclosed identity is defended because uncertainty feels more threatening than limitation. The protocol works not by challenging the identity but by introducing small, low-stakes exceptions to it.

hypervigilance.name: Hypervigilance
hypervigilance.description: Hypervigilance is a chronic state of threat-scanning in which the nervous system remains on alert even in safe environments. It developed as an accurate response to an unpredictable environment and became a default setting. The cost is exhaustion, difficulty being present, and interpreting neutral events as threatening.
hypervigilance.protocol_note: Hypervigilance cannot be switched off by reasoning — it is a body state, not a thought. The intervention must be somatic before it can be cognitive.
